openings.claim: The shelving routine may manufacture demand for exception tracking and corrective searches: moving holds after the slip is completed makes its pointers stale, leading to second-location searches and further correction work. This evaluates a bounded location-freeze probe; any lasting intervention remains unproven.
openings.delta: Remove the post-recording transfer link for existing cart holds and recorded exceptions during a stipulated evening window, retaining their current storage addresses rather than assuming shelving speeds retrieval.
openings.prediction: Compared with comparable ordinary evenings, frozen holds should have fewer stale slip entries and fewer second-location searches or pickups exceeding two minutes, including during the arrival burst, while correct-reader handoffs remain intact.
openings.rival_prediction: Household-surname misfiling is the nearest alternative: freezing locations improves slip accuracy but second searches and delays persist, particularly for household-name mismatches, because the book already has the wrong primary address.
openings.defeat: If the freeze is maintained and entries stay accurate, but second searches and delays remain comparable and concentrate on household-name mismatches, the proposed transfer-to-delay explanation loses support. Any wrong-reader handoff defeats practical success.

Keep identifying paperwork behind the desk and retain normal reader verification. Record actual movements, stale entries, household-name mismatches, search locations, elapsed pickup times and handoff errors; compare comparable ordinary evenings by peak interval. Keep total daily preparation within ten clerk-minutes, including probe preparation. Assess the 95% within-two-minutes target and zero wrong-reader handoffs; no benefit is stipulated.
